decisions: Matrices and methods require v5/v6; v1-v4 receive explicit MATRIX_VERSION diagnostics.
Primitive int/float/bool/string, nominal enums and flat UDT; no graphics/color, nested collections, matrix requests.
Numeric reductions select the element type except rank, which returns int. Mode picks the smallest tied value. Trace reads the square diagonal and propagates missing diagonal values.
Arithmetic promotes mixed numeric operands to float; matrix times vector returns an array. All results use independent buffers.
Square accepts any admitted matrix. Nine value predicates require numeric elements. Structural predicates require square shape except binary and zero.
Stochastic requires a nonempty square matrix with each row nonnegative and summing to one after accurate float summation. Required missing values fail comparisons.
Half-open submatrix creates independent slots; concat appends rows into id1 and returns its identity. Reverse rotates both axes.
Sort reorders complete rows stably using the existing order tokens and missing-key bucket. V6 UDT sorting uses a closed field name/index, default zero.
Kronecker products expand row-major blocks with numeric promotion. Powers use nonnegative integer exponents on square matrices; power zero returns the identity.
Binary exponentiation scans exponent bits from the most significant, rounding and range-checking each completed matrix product.
Determinant and rank use partial pivoting. Integer elimination uses exact divisions; float rank normalizes by the largest magnitude and discards pivots at or below max(rows,columns)*2^-52.
Missing cells propagate to both results. The empty determinant is one; empty rank is zero. Only the determinant requires a square matrix.
Inverse uses pivoted LU for float, exact elimination for int. Fractional int results and singular matrices receive distinct diagnostics. Missing cells fill the result with missing values.
Float pseudoinverse uses scaled one-sided Jacobi SVD; cutoff is largest singular value times max dimension times machine epsilon. Full-rank squares reuse inverse.
Integer pseudoinverse requires integral orthogonal projectors; invert the supported coordinate block exactly and scatter it into the transposed shape.
Real eigensystems are sorted by increasing eigenvalue. Integer eigenvalues and primitive integer basis columns are exact. Complex spectra and incomplete eigenbases have explicit diagnostics.
Dense row-major buffers share existing heap IDs and global quotas; each dimension is bounded by100000, product by100000. Zero dimensions are retained.
Only0x0 infers the opposite extent from an inserted array. Omitted vectors insert typed missing, bool false in v6.
Remove defaults to the last valid index. Frozen Wiki v5 spells rows/columns, which would be out of bounds; see ADR0003.
Row/col/copy/transpose have independent containers and shallow shared UDT aliases; remove returns an independent array.
Iteration snapshots shape/row count, reads an independent row immediately before each iteration, and fails next iteration after shape changes. This is a bounded interpretation.
Mutations stage the whole buffer. Remove preflights the final buffer and returned vector together; existing work/memory/storage/cancellation limits apply.
Matrix programs use typed-ir.18/runtime-state.11/array-heap.4 with packed UDT IDs; imported bundles and old program formats remain unchanged.
